KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: To ensure that all visitors and telephone callers to the practice are greeted professionally. To ensure all telephone calls are managed appropriately. To manage the flow of patients arriving at the reception desk, for appointments, prescriptions, or queries. To ensure the clinical staffs receive medical records as requested. To ensure that repeat prescriptions are generated accurately and efficiently, within the 48 hours specified by the practice. KEY TASKS: Reception duties: Greeting and booking in or patients for surgeries and clinics. Dealing with patient enquiries efficiently and courteously. The receiving and recording of telephone messages taking appropriate action. Making appointments on EMIS Clinical System, by processing appointment requests for today, future appointments from patients in person and on the telephone. You will play an important part in ensuring that the practice runs smoothly, supporting the wider team and helping to make sure that administrative processes are completed in a timely and organised manner. This is a varied and rewarding role for someone who is organised, reliable and has excellent attention to detail. You will need to be confident working in a busy environment, able to manage competing priorities and have good communication and IT skills. We value our staff, encourage learning and development, and recognise the important contribution every member of the team makes to providing safe, effective and compassionate patient care. The role will involve providing administrative support across a range of practice functions, with particular responsibility for coordinating safeguarding administration. This will include maintaining safeguarding records, monitoring actions and ensuring relevant information is accurately recorded and followed up. The postholder will be responsible for managing patient recalls and monitoring outstanding actions to ensure patients are invited for appropriate reviews and follow-up. They will also support clinical and administrative audits, including gathering information, updating records and monitoring progress against agreed actions. Other duties will include clinical and administrative coding, maintaining accurate patient information, processing correspondence, preparing reports and supporting the practice with routine data management. The role will also involve providing administrative support for practice meetings, including preparing agendas, taking minutes, recording decisions and maintaining action logs to ensure agreed actions are followed through. The successful candidate will need to be highly organised, methodical and able to manage their own workload, ensuring that important deadlines, reviews and follow-up actions are not missed. Confidentiality, accuracy and good attention to detail are essential. Main Purpose of the Role To provide comprehensive administrative support to the practice, with specific responsibility for safeguarding administration, patient recalls, clinical and administrative audits and maintaining accurate patient records. The postholder will support the smooth day-to-day running of the practice, working closely with clinical and non-clinical colleagues to ensure that administrative processes are completed accurately, efficiently and within agreed timescales. Act as the practice Safeguarding Administration Lead, providing administrative support to the clinical safeguarding leads. Maintain and update safeguarding registers and records for adults and children. Ensure safeguarding information and relevant documentation are accurately recorded and appropriately filed within patient records. Monitor safeguarding correspondence, referrals and incoming information, ensuring these are brought to the attention of the appropriate clinician. Maintain safeguarding action logs and monitor outstanding administrative actions. Support the organisation of safeguarding meetings and multidisciplinary discussions. Ensure relevant safeguarding documentation is processed and shared appropriately, in accordance with practice procedures and information governance requirements. Escalate any safeguarding concerns or urgent correspondence promptly to the appropriate clinical lead. Provide administrative support for the practice recall system. Identify and contact patients requiring reviews, investigations, monitoring or follow-up. Monitor outstanding recalls and maintain accurate records of invitations and patient responses. Follow up patients who have not responded to invitations in accordance with practice protocols. Support the monitoring of patients requiring regular reviews for long-term conditions and other clinical requirements. Assist with DNA (Did Not Attend) management, identifying missed appointments and supporting appropriate follow-up. Maintain accurate recall information and report any outstanding issues to the relevant clinical team. Lead and undertake practice audits as directed by the Practice Manager and clinical leads. Identify patients and gather relevant information for audit purposes. Extract, collate and accurately record data from clinical systems. Prepare audit reports and present findings where required. Maintain audit records and action plans, monitoring progress against agreed actions. Support the practice with clinical governance activities and quality improvement initiatives. Assist with the collection of evidence for enhanced services, contractual requirements and CQC compliance. Input relevant information into patient healthcare records accurately and in a timely manner. Undertake clinical coding of incoming correspondence, documents and other information in accordance with practice protocols and training. Process hospital letters, clinical correspondence and other patient documentation, ensuring information is directed appropriately. Maintain accurate patient demographic and registration information. Reception duties: Ensure an effective and efficient reception service is provided to patients and any other visitors to the Practice. Deal with all general enquiries, explain procedures and make new and follow-up appointments. Using your own judgment and communication skills ensure that patients with no prior appointment but who need urgent consultation are seen in a logical and non-disruptive manner. Explain Practice arrangements and formal requirements to new patients and those seeking temporary cover and ensure procedures are completed. Receive and make telephone calls as required. Divert calls and take messages, ensuring accuracy of detail and prompt appropriate delivery. Enter requests for home visits into the home visits book, ensuring careful recording of all relevant details and where necessary refer to Duty Doctor. Action repeat prescription requests and ensure that they are ready for collection by the patient within 72 hours, in line with Practice protocol. Take action on clinicians requests for further information/patient contact information etc. (including computerised practice notes), ensuring completion of all associated paperwork. Advise patients of relevant charges for private (non-General Medical Services) services, accept payment and issue receipts for same. Enter patient information on to the computer as required. Ensure that all new patients are registered onto the computer system promptly and accurately Make and serve refreshments for meetings, ensure the kitchen is kept clean and tidy and air and tidy the waiting room in turn with other staff. Covering colleagues holiday and sick cover as required. Process incoming and outgoing mail according to practice protocols. Record actions taken in patient record where appropriate or in accordance with practice protocols. title: Practice Administrator
description: We are looking for an organised, motivated and proactive individual to join The Wapping Group Practice and take the lead in managing our QOF, LES and patient recall systems. This is a temporary maternity cover position, with a fixed-term contract of at least 13 months. Flexible working hours: 25 to 37.5 hours per week . This is an important role within our practice, ensuring patients receive the care they need while helping us achieve our clinical and contractual targets. You will work closely with our clinical, administrative and PCN teams to coordinate recalls, monitor performance, improve processes and ensure accurate clinical coding. We offer a friendly and supportive working environment where you will have the opportunity to take ownership of your work, develop your skills and make a real difference to patient care and practice performance. We will provide the necessary training and support to help you succeed in this role, so you do not need to have experience in every aspect of the job. We are looking for someone who is willing to learn, takes initiative and is committed to delivering high-quality work. The successful candidate will be responsible for overseeing the practice's QOF, LES and patient recall systems, ensuring patients are contacted, booked and followed up appropriately. The role involves monitoring performance against clinical targets, coordinating recall activities with the administrative and PCN teams, managing appointment availability and ensuring accurate clinical coding on EMIS. You will also oversee childhood immunisation and cervical screening recalls, identify areas for improvement and work closely with the clinical team to maximise practice performance. Key Responsibilities QOF, LES and Target Management Manage and coordinate all QOF, LES and other contractual recall activities to ensure the practice achieves maximum performance against targets. Monitor QOF and LES dashboards regularly, identifying areas where performance needs improvement. Take responsibility for managing all targets comprehensively, ensuring patients are recalled, booked and appropriately coded. Regularly update EMIS searches and review performance dashboards to identify outstanding work and missed opportunities. Work closely with the clinical and administrative teams to ensure all targets are achieved within the required deadlines. Patient Recall Management Manage the practice's recall system from start to finish, ensuring eligible patients are identified, contacted, booked and followed up. Generate, distribute and monitor recall lists, ensuring work is completed accurately and on time. Allocate recall lists to PCN recall staff, monitor their progress and follow up on outstanding tasks. Ensure patients who do not respond to initial recall attempts are followed up appropriately. Send validation letters to patients who have not responded after repeated contact attempts, in line with practice protocols. Ensure accurate records are maintained of all recall attempts, patient responses and outcomes. Clinical Appointment Management Review and adjust clinical appointment sessions on EMIS, adding or removing appointment slots where necessary to support QOF and LES recall activities. Ensure sufficient clinical appointments are available for patients requiring reviews, monitoring, vaccinations and other target-related activities. Liaise with clinicians and the management team to plan appointment capacity according to recall demand and outstanding targets. Clinical Coding and Data Quality Ensure all QOF and LES activities are accurately coded on EMIS to support correct reporting and achievement. Identify missing or incorrect clinical codes and liaise with the relevant clinicians to resolve any issues. Provide training and guidance to administrative and recall staff on correct clinical coding procedures. Keep staff updated on changes to QOF, LES and other relevant coding requirements. Carry out regular data quality checks to ensure completed clinical activities are correctly recorded and reflected in performance reports. Childhood Immunisations and Cervical Screening Manage childhood immunisation recalls and targets, ensuring eligible children are identified, contacted and followed up. Monitor childhood immunisation performance and work with the clinical team to improve uptake and achieve contractual targets. Manage cervical screening recalls comprehensively, ensuring eligible patients are invited, booked and appropriately followed up. Monitor cervical screening uptake and identify patients who are overdue or have not responded to invitations. Ensure cervical screening records are accurately maintained, including coding of colposcopy correspondence and relevant clinical outcomes. Ensure cervical screening referral information is correctly recorded and processed through CSMS where required. Work closely with the clinical team to resolve coding discrepancies and ensure screening activity is accurately reflected in EMIS and performance dashboards. Staff Coordination and Training Coordinate the work of PCN recall staff by allocating tasks, setting priorities and monitoring progress. Provide regular feedback and guidance to ensure recall activities are completed efficiently. Train staff on recall procedures, EMIS searches, clinical coding and changes to contractual requirements. Maintain effective communication between clinical, administrative and PCN teams to ensure a coordinated approach to achieving practice targets. Identify areas for improvement and implement changes to strengthen recall processes and overall performance. Performance Monitoring and Reporting Regularly review QOF, LES, childhood immunisation and cervical screening performance. Identify gaps in achievement and take proactive steps to improve performance before contractual deadlines. Provide regular progress updates to the Practice Manager, highlighting outstanding targets, risks and areas requiring additional support. Ensure the practice maximises appropriate contractual achievement and income through effective recall management, accurate coding and timely completion of clinical activities.
